title: ‘हामी नै स्टेट हौँ र मेरो इच्छा नै कानुन हो भन्ने भ्रम सरकारले नपाले हुन्छ’ (भिडिओ)
content:
No ads found for this position काठमाडौं । नेपाली कांग्रेसका सभापति गगन थापाले लोकतन्त्र, नागरिक अधिकार र प्रेस स्वतन्त्रतामाथि सरकारले सीमा नाघेको भन्दै कांग्रेस चुप लागेर नबस्ने चेतावनी दिएका छन् । समाचार लेखेकै आधारमा सञ्चारगृहभित्रै प्रवेश गरेर पत्रकार पक्राउ गर्ने सरकारी कदमले शाही शासनकालको झल्को दिएको भन्दै उनले यसको सशक्त प्रतिवाद गर्ने बताए । सानेपास्थित कांग्रेस मुख्यालयमा विशेष सम्बोधन गर्दै थापाले पछिल्लो समय पत्रकार पक्राउ प्रकरणमा प्रधानमन्त्रीको सचिवालय र प्रहरीको गतिविधि विचित्र र शङ्कास्पद देखिएको टिप्पणी गरे । ‘पहिले प्रहरीले पत्रकार पक्राउ गर्‍यो, प्रधानमन्त्रीको सचिवालयबाट ‘हामीलाई केही थाहा छैन’ भन्ने वक्तव्य आयो । फेरि प्रहरीले मध्यराति प्रधानमन्त्री कार्यालयको चासोलाई सम्बोधन गर्न पक्राउ गरिएको भन्यो र शनिबार बिहान त्यो वक्तव्य पनि डिलिट गरियो,’ थापाले भने, ‘अहिले त प्रधानमन्त्रीकै सचिवालयबाट २८ जना पत्रकारको सूची बनाएर प्रहरीकहाँ पठाइएको विषय बाहिर आइसकेको छ ।’ पत्रकार पक्राउ पर्नु र रिहा हुनुमै यो विषय नटुङ्गिने स्पष्ट पार्दै उनले थपे, ‘पत्रकार पक्राउ परे, छुटे, अब सकियो भन्ने होइन । यतिमै विषय सकिँदैन र सक्किनु पनि हुँदैन भन्ने कांग्रेसको स्पष्ट धारणा छ । यसले सरकारले राज्य, नागरिक अधिकार र प्रेस स्वतन्त्रतालाई कसरी बुझेको छ भन्ने गम्भीर प्रश्न खडा गरेको छ ।’ प्रहरी आफैँ निर्णय गरेर मिडिया हाउस नगएको ठोकुवा गर्दै थापाले सत्ताको सनक र सामाजिक सञ्जालको प्रतिक्रियाका आधारमा राज्य चलाउन खोजिएको आरोप लगाए । उनको व्यंग्य थियो, ‘केही साथीहरू बसेर समाचार हेर्दै ल केटाहरू, यी ८/१० जनालाई उठाइदे भन्नुभयो होला । फेरि एकछिनपछि अर्को साथीले ए, लाइक घट्यो घट्यो, छाड्दे छाड्दे’ भन्यो । यो प्रवृत्ति अत्यन्तै चिन्ताजनक छ ।’ सरकारमा रहेकाहरूमा ‘हामी नै राज्य (स्टेट) हौँ’ भन्ने अहङ्कार पलाएको गगनको टिप्पणी छ । उनले भने, ‘हामीले बोलेको कुरा हुकुम हुन्छ भन्ने ठानेर राज्यका निकाय र शक्तिको स्वेच्छाचारी प्रयोग भइरहेको छ । सरकारमा बसेकाहरूलाई मेरो इच्छा नै कानुन हो भन्ने लाग्न थालेपछि समस्या सुरु हुन्छ । यसलाई सामान्यीकरण गर्न मिल्दैन, अब हद नाघेको छ ।’ Kathmandu. Nepali Congress President Gagan Thapa has warned that the Congress will not remain silent, saying that the government has crossed the line on democracy, civil rights and press freedom. He said that the government's move to enter a media house and arrest journalists based on writing news gave a glimpse of the royal rule and said that it would strongly oppose it. Addressing a special address at the Nepali Congress headquarters in Sanepa, Thapa commented that the recent activities of the Prime Minister's Secretariat and the police in the arrest of journalists appear strange and suspicious. "First the police arrested the journalist, and the Prime Minister's Secretariat issued a statement saying 'we don't know anything'. Then the police said at midnight that the arrests were made to address the concerns of the Prime Minister's Office, and that statement was also deleted on Saturday morning," Thapa said. "Now, it has come to light that the Prime Minister's Secretariat prepared a list of 28 journalists and sent them to the police." Making it clear that the issue will not be resolved by the arrest and release of journalists, he added, "It does not mean that the issue is over just because the journalists are arrested and released. The Congress is of the clear view that the issue cannot and should not be resolved by this. This has raised serious questions about how the government understands the state, civil rights and press freedom." Stating that the police did not go to the media house on their own decision, Thapa accused the government of trying to run the state based on the whims of the government and the reactions of social media. His sarcasm was, 'Some friends were sitting watching the news and said, "Hey guys, pick up these 8/10 people." Then after a while, another friend said, "Hey, the likes are decreasing, they're decreasing, they're quitting." This trend is very worrying.' Gagan comments that those in government have developed an arrogance that says, "We are the state." He said, "State bodies and power are being used arbitrarily, thinking that what we say is a command. The problem begins when those in government start thinking that my will is the law. This cannot be generalized, it has now crossed the line."

Nepali Congress President Gagan Thapa has warned that the Congress will not remain silent, saying that the government has crossed the line on democracy, civil rights and press freedom. He said that the government's move to enter a media house and arrest journalists based on writing news gave a glimpse of the royal rule and said that it would strongly oppose it. Addressing a special address at the Nepali Congress headquarters in Sanepa, Thapa commented that the recent activities of the Prime Minister's Secretariat and the police in the arrest of journalists appear strange and suspicious. "First the police arrested the journalist, and the Prime Minister's Secretariat issued a statement saying 'we don't know anything'. Then the police said at midnight that the arrests were made to address the concerns of the Prime Minister's Office, and that statement was also deleted on Saturday morning," Thapa said. "Now, it has come to light that the Prime Minister's Secretariat prepared a list of 28 journalists and sent them to the police." Making it clear that the issue will not be resolved by the arrest and release of journalists, he added, "It does not mean that the issue is over just because the journalists are arrested and released. The Congress is of the clear view that the issue cannot and should not be resolved by this. This has raised serious questions about how the government understands the state, civil rights and press freedom." Stating that the police did not go to the media house on their own decision, Thapa accused the government of trying to run the state based on the whims of the government and the reactions of social media. His sarcasm was, 'Some friends were sitting watching the news and said, "Hey guys, pick up these 8/10 people." Then after a while, another friend said, "Hey, the likes are decreasing, they're decreasing, they're quitting." This trend is very worrying.' Gagan comments that those in government have developed an arrogance that says, "We are the state." He said, "State bodies and power are being used arbitrarily, thinking that what we say is a command. The problem begins when those in government start thinking that my will is the law. This cannot be generalized, it has now crossed the line."

प्रहरी आफैँ निर्णय गरेर मिडिया हाउस नगएको ठोकुवा गर्दै थापाले सत्ताको सनक र सामाजिक सञ्जालको प्रतिक्रियाका आधारमा राज्य चलाउन खोजिएको आरोप लगाए ।

उनको व्यंग्य थियो, ‘केही साथीहरू बसेर समाचार हेर्दै ल केटाहरू, यी ८/१० जनालाई उठाइदे भन्नुभयो होला । फेरि एकछिनपछि अर्को साथीले ए, लाइक घट्यो घट्यो, छाड्दे छाड्दे’ भन्यो । यो प्रवृत्ति अत्यन्तै चिन्ताजनक छ ।’

सरकारमा रहेकाहरूमा ‘हामी नै राज्य (स्टेट) हौँ’ भन्ने अहङ्कार पलाएको गगनको टिप्पणी छ ।

उनले भने, ‘हामीले बोलेको कुरा हुकुम हुन्छ भन्ने ठानेर राज्यका निकाय र शक्तिको स्वेच्छाचारी प्रयोग भइरहेको छ । सरकारमा बसेकाहरूलाई मेरो इच्छा नै कानुन हो भन्ने लाग्न थालेपछि समस्या सुरु हुन्छ । यसलाई सामान्यीकरण गर्न मिल्दैन, अब हद नाघेको छ ।’

Kathmandu. Nepali Congress President Gagan Thapa has warned that the Congress will not remain silent, saying that the government has crossed the line on democracy, civil rights and press freedom. He said that the government's move to enter a media house and arrest journalists based on writing news gave a glimpse of the royal rule and said that it would strongly oppose it. Addressing a special address at the Nepali Congress headquarters in Sanepa, Thapa commented that the recent activities of the Prime Minister's Secretariat and the police in the arrest of journalists appear strange and suspicious. "First the police arrested the journalist, and the Prime Minister's Secretariat issued a statement saying 'we don't know anything'. Then the police said at midnight that the arrests were made to address the concerns of the Prime Minister's Office, and that statement was also deleted on Saturday morning," Thapa said. "Now, it has come to light that the Prime Minister's Secretariat prepared a list of 28 journalists and sent them to the police." Making it clear that the issue will not be resolved by the arrest and release of journalists, he added, "It does not mean that the issue is over just because the journalists are arrested and released. The Congress is of the clear view that the issue cannot and should not be resolved by this. This has raised serious questions about how the government understands the state, civil rights and press freedom." Stating that the police did not go to the media house on their own decision, Thapa accused the government of trying to run the state based on the whims of the government and the reactions of social media. His sarcasm was, 'Some friends were sitting watching the news and said, "Hey guys, pick up these 8/10 people." Then after a while, another friend said, "Hey, the likes are decreasing, they're decreasing, they're quitting." This trend is very worrying.' Gagan comments that those in government have developed an arrogance that says, "We are the state." He said, "State bodies and power are being used arbitrarily, thinking that what we say is a command. The problem begins when those in government start thinking that my will is the law. This cannot be generalized, it has now crossed the line."
